sections.h2: Where is Prattville, Alabama, and which counties does it cover?
sections.html:
Prattville is the county seat of Autauga County, and the city also extends into Elmore County. It lies northwest of Montgomery and is part of the Montgomery metropolitan area.

The city covers about 36 square miles at roughly 276 feet of elevation. Interstate 65 runs north to south east of downtown, with access from exits 179 and 181, both of which are in the Elmore County part of the city. The highway leads 14 miles southeast to downtown Montgomery and 82 miles north to Birmingham.

The split between two counties is not a footnote for a seller. Which county holds your parcel can affect which school system serves the address, and it is worth confirming before you advertise anything.

sections.h2: How did Prattville begin, and what is it known for?
sections.html:
Daniel Pratt, an industrialist and architect from Temple, New Hampshire, founded Prattville in 1839. He bought roughly 1,000 acres from Joseph May at $21 an acre and built his manufacturing works and the town along Autauga Creek, because the creek could power his cotton gin equipment.

The town became the county seat of Autauga County in 1868. It is nicknamed the Fountain City for the many artesian wells in the area, and its motto is "The Preferred Community." The Daniel Pratt Historic District, Bell House and Buena Vista are all on the National Register of Historic Places.

A downtown house near the old mill district may be more than a century old.

Prattville had 37,781 residents at the 2020 census and a Census Bureau estimate of 40,582 for 2025, a rise of 7.4 percent. The population was only 13,116 in 1970.

The 2020 census counted 14,624 households and 15,537 housing units, of which 5.9 percent were vacant. The homeowner vacancy rate was 1.3 percent and the rental vacancy rate was 5.9 percent.

The median age in Prattville was 37.6 years at the 2020 census, and 24.4 percent of residents were under 18. Married couples headed 50.3 percent of households, and 34.9 percent of households had children under 18.

About 25.4 percent of households were one person living alone, and 10.0 percent were a person 65 or older living alone. The city is mostly urban, with 92.7 percent of residents in urban areas.

sections.h2: What local landmarks and community details come up in Prattville?
sections.html:
Prattville has a mix of industrial heritage and newer recreation. Beyond the National Register sites, a historical marker on 6th Street honors Happy Hollow, a steep hill that turns into a curve and was the center of African American life in Prattville in the 1950s.

Golf is part of the city's identity as well. The Senator Course at Capitol Hill hosted the LPGA Tour's Navistar (now Yokohama Tire) LPGA Classic from 2007 through 2012. The Prattville Progress, a twice-weekly newspaper, covers local news, and the city belongs to the Montgomery television market.

When you explain your house to a buyer from outside the area, these anchors help: the creek and old mill sites downtown, the interstate exits on the east side and the shopping at High Point Town Center.

Most of Prattville, meaning the Autauga County portion, belongs to the Autauga County School System, which has eight schools in the city including Prattville High School and the Autauga County Technology Center. The Elmore County part of the city is in the Elmore County Public School System.

Prattville Christian Academy and Autauga Academy are private schools based in the city. Because of the county line, the same city can mean two different districts, so check the address before quoting a school zone to a buyer. The district offices are the authority on that.

sections.h2: What roads and transit connect Prattville to the rest of Alabama?
sections.html:
Interstate 65, U.S. 31, U.S. 82 and State Route 14 all pass through the city. U.S. 82 runs south with I-65 toward downtown Montgomery and leads northwest 89 miles to Tuscaloosa.

  • I-65 gives fast access to Montgomery and, farther north, Birmingham.
  • A small airport lies about 3.5 miles from downtown.
  • Autauga County Rural Transportation runs a dial-a-ride service in the city and county.
  • The Prattville Fire Department and Police Department serve the city.

Prattville is also home to High Point Town Center, a large shopping center built in 2007 and 2008, and to the Capitol Hill golf courses on the Robert Trent Jones Golf Trail. Stanley-Jensen Stadium holds about 10,000 people.

sections.h2: What happened in the 2008 Prattville tornado?
sections.html:
An EF3 tornado hit Prattville on February 17, 2008, and destroyed more than 45 homes and businesses while damaging over 700 others. Twenty-nine people were hurt and none died, and preliminary damage estimates reached $85 million across insured and uninsured losses.

Houses repaired after that storm may carry paperwork worth keeping, such as permits, contractor invoices and insurance records. A buyer or an inspector may ask for it. If you own a house with an unrepaired roof or wall from any later storm, say so plainly, since hidden damage usually comes out during inspection.

Prattville has a humid subtropical climate.

sections.h2: What taxes and fees apply when a Prattville house is sold?
sections.html:
The Alabama Department of Revenue says property taxes are due October 1 and delinquent after December 31. A sale that closes between those dates should settle any unpaid balance.

Under Alabama Code section 40-22-1, a deed cannot be recorded until the recordation tax is paid. The rate is 50 cents for each $500 of value or fraction of $500, so a $240,000 sale produces 480 units, or $240, before the recording fee. Two thirds of the tax goes to the state and one third to the county.

The statute also requires proof of the actual price, on a form the Alabama Department of Revenue prepares. A person who intentionally fails to give that proof after a request, or gives false proof, owes a penalty of $100 or 25 percent of the tax due, whichever is greater. A seller who gives the closing agent an accurate contract avoids that issue.

sections.h2: When does a cash sale make sense for a Prattville owner?
sections.html:
A cash sale suits owners who want a fixed closing date or who do not want to prepare a house for showings. Typical cases in Prattville include:

  • An older house near the historic district that needs roofing, wiring or plumbing work.
  • A rental where the tenant moved out and left repairs behind.
  • An inherited house in either Autauga or Elmore County.
  • A family relocating for work toward Montgomery or Birmingham on a short timetable.

We buy Prattville houses as they are. You can ask for an offer, compare it with a listing plan, and decide what suits you.

faqs.q: What county is Prattville, Alabama, in?
faqs.a: Prattville is the county seat of Autauga County, and part of the city lies in Elmore County.

faqs.q: Why is Prattville called the Fountain City?
faqs.a: Wikipedia says the nickname comes from the many artesian wells in the area.
Industrialist Daniel Pratt founded the town in 1839 along Autauga Creek.

faqs.q: How far is Prattville from Montgomery?
faqs.a: Interstate 65 leads about 14 miles southeast from the city to downtown Montgomery.

faqs.q: When are Prattville property taxes due?
faqs.a: Alabama property taxes are due October 1 and delinquent after December 31, according to the state Department of Revenue.

faqs.q: What is the population of Prattville?
faqs.a: The 2020 census counted 37,781 residents, and the Census Bureau estimated 40,582 for 2025.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Prattville house with storm damage?
faqs.a: Yes. We buy houses in Prattville as they are, including those with roof or storm damage.
